title: ResourceLoader load performance regression (compared to 3.5.3)
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: Godot 4.4.1 - Not reproducible in: Godot 3.5.3 ### System information Godot v4.4.1.stable (9a3480ff1) - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7283) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) ### Issue description In some circumstances, `ResourceLoader.load()` and friends (`ResourceLoader.load_threaded_get()`, `@GDScript.load()`) is vastly slower than the Godot 3.5.3 counterparts. Notably, if `ResourceLoader.load()` attempts to load a scene with a script, which in turn references a different script (e.g. a global/autoload script, or a script with a `class_name`), the load time is drastically impacted. The degree of impact seems to be related to non-blank lines of code (when running from editor, commented out lines also have an effect, after export these are seemingly stripped and do not impact anything). While Godot 3.5 does seem to be slightly impacted, Godot 4.4 is massively impacted, at least 2x in our testing. This is seemingly made worse if there are multiple sub-scenes, each with a script referencing the "high-cost" script. Seemingly every scene/script pays a price of parsing the script. In terms of real world numbers/impact, our game project sees a roughly 5x increase in purely loading time, from roughly 2 seconds in Godot 3.5.3, to roughly 10 seconds in Godot 4.4.1. These numbers are using exported versions of the game. Attached are 2 minimum reproduction projects, 1 made in Godot 3.5.3, and 1 made in Godot 4.4.1. They are set up identically. ### Steps to reproduce Two projects are included: * ResourceLoader_3_5 * ResourceLoader_4_4 Both have identical setup. 1) Happy Example The `Load Scene` button loads a scene (loaded_scene_without_script.tscn) which does not have a script attached to it. 2) Sad Example The `Load Scene (with script reference)` button loads `loaded_scene_with_script.tscn`, which uses `loaded_scene_with_script.gd`. This script has a reference to `HorribleScript`, defined in `horrible_script.gd` 3) Very Sad Example The `Load Scene (with 2x script reference)` button loads `loaded_scene_with_double_script.tscn`, which uses `loaded_scene_with_double_script.gd`. This script has a reference to `HorribleScript`, defined in `horrible_script.gd`. In addition, it also includes a sub-scene `loaded_scene_with_script.tscn`, which in turn has a script referencing the same `HorribleScript` In short, both the loaded scene and one of its sub-scenes contains a reference to the same script. Note that, due to caching, only `Sad example` or `Very sad example` can be loaded in 1 session. Restart the project to compare. Note that the difference seems to be worse after exporting than when running in editor. | Godot 3.5.3 Sad | Godot 3.5.3 Very Sad | | ------------------ | ----------------------- | | | | | Godot 4.4.1 Sad | Godot 4.4.1 Very Sad | | ------------------ | ----------------------- | | | | ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) The issue can be reproduced both by running in the editor, and/or via running an exported version. [ResourceLoader_3_5.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21672585/ResourceLoader_3_5.zip) [ResourceLoader_4_4.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21672586/ResourceLoader_4_4.zip)
